steps.title: Prepare recording and suction electrodes
steps.instruction: Pull suction pipettes to an opening of ~5 µm and recording electrodes to a resistance of ~15 MΩ; polish the suction tip with the micro‑forge; fill both recording micropipettes with 3 mM KCl and fill the suction pipette with 3 mM Ca²⁺‑modified HL‑3 saline using a micro‑fill needle and a 10 mL syringe.

substeps.instruction: Fill recording pipettes with 3 mM KCl.
Fill suction pipette with 3 mM Ca²⁺‑modified HL‑3 using micro‑fill and syringe.

steps.title: Assemble magnetic recording chamber
steps.instruction: Use a 3" × 4" glass chamber, cut a diamond‑shaped opening in magnetic tape placed in the centre, and seal the tape edges to the glass with a glue gun; this chamber holds saline around the dissected larva. (A 60 mm Sylgard‑lined dish with pins can be used as an alternative, but the magnetic chamber is preferred.)

steps.title: Prepare Ca²⁺‑free HL‑3 saline
steps.instruction: Make modified HL‑3 solution without CaCl₂ (same composition as HL‑3 below, omit CaCl₂); store the Ca²⁺‑free solution at –20 °C and thaw before use.

steps.title: Dissect third‑instar larvae
steps.instruction: Place third‑instar larvae in ice‑cold Ca²⁺‑free HL‑3 to prevent muscle movement; loosely pin them in the magnetic chamber, remove guts, trachea and ventral nerve cord, cut all motor nerves from the ventral nerve cord, and perfuse several times with fresh HL‑3 saline. Ensure motor nerves are not cut too short. Fill the chamber with 3 mM Ca²⁺‑modified HL‑3 saline and orient the preparation so that muscle 6 (segments A2 or A3) is optimally positioned for electrode access.

steps.title: Position electrodes and establish suction seal
steps.instruction: Under a 4× objective, place the larval preparation and the three electrodes in the centre of the field and lower them toward the preparation. Switch to a 40× objective, bring muscle 6 close to the electrodes, lower the suction electrode near the nerve bundle, apply a small negative pressure through the syringe to withdraw the nerve into the pipette, and use suction to form a seal between the suction electrode and the motor nerve.

steps.title: Set recording baseline and filter
steps.instruction: Reset bridge balance and pipette offset to set electrode baseline potentials to 0 mV; if the pipette offset exceeds 100 mV, chlorinate the silver wire in the recording pipette. Digitize electrophysiological sweeps at 10 kHz and apply a 1 kHz low‑pass filter in Clampex.

steps.title: Measure resting potential and input resistance
steps.instruction: Impale muscle 6 with the voltage‑follower electrode (HS‑9Ax0.1) and record the resting potential (Vrest). Inject a 500 ms pulse of –1 nA to determine input resistance (Rin = (Vrest – (–1 nA)) / current) by Ohm’s law. Discard recordings where Vrest is more depolarized than –60 mV or more hyperpolarized than –85 mV, or where Rin < 5 MΩ.

steps.title: Stabilize and clamp muscle for TEVC
steps.instruction: Impale the same fiber with the current‑injection electrode (HS‑13Sx10) and wait 15–20 s until voltage readings from both electrodes stabilize at more hyperpolarized than –55 mV. Switch to two‑electrode voltage‑clamp (TEVC) mode, clamp the membrane at –70 mV, and monitor leak current; reject the preparation if leak current exceeds 10 nA.

steps.title: Record miniature EPSCs
steps.instruction: Record miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) for one minute in the absence of any stimulation, using a gain setting of 80.

steps.title: Stimulate motor axons for EPSCs
steps.instruction: Use an ISO‑Flex stimulus isolator (A.M.P.I.) to deliver current pulses to the motor axon; adjust stimulus intensity for each recording so that both neurons innervating muscle 6 fire consistently, avoiding overstimulation that produces multiple‑peak responses.

steps.title: Run RRP stimulation protocol
steps.instruction: With the same optimal stimulus intensity, apply a 60 Hz train of 30 stimuli in 3 mM extracellular Ca²⁺ HL‑3; repeat the train five times per recording to generate progressive EPSC depression.

steps.title: Analyze cumulative EPSC to estimate RRP
steps.instruction: Plot cumulative EPSC amplitude versus time, fit a straight line to the data from stimuli 18–30, extrapolate the line back to time 0, and divide the y‑intercept by the average mEPSC amplitude to obtain the readily releasable pool size.

steps.title: Prepare recording electrode solution
steps.instruction: Make a recording electrode solution containing 3 M KCl.
